@@139296301 <h> Thank you for registering <h> Scared exercise will injure you ? These rules make any routine safe <p> One reader joked that following Harry Bullmore 's advice landed them in A&amp;E . It 's a laugh -- but it points to a real fear . In the latest Well Enough newsletter , he breaks down the two principles that make sure exercise never has that effect , whatever your starting point <h> Bookmark popover <h> Your support helps us to tell the story <p> From reproductive rights to climate change to Big Tech , The Independent is on the ground when the story is developing . Whether it 's investigating the financials of Elon Musk 's pro-Trump PAC or producing our latest documentary , ' The A Word ' , which shines a light on the American women fighting for reproductive rights , we know how important it is to parse out the facts from the messaging . <p> At such a critical moment in US history , we need reporters on the ground . Your donation allows us to keep sending journalists to speak to both sides of @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ across the entire political spectrum . And unlike many other quality news outlets , we choose not to lock Americans out of our reporting and analysis with paywalls . We believe quality journalism should be available to everyone , paid for by those who can afford it . <p> Your support makes all the difference . <p> I recently wrote a feature on bone strength and how to increase it , hoping to help people swerve injury and stay mobile for longer . The key , experts say , is to challenge the body with exercises like running , jumping and lifting , which place load on the bones and prompt them to adapt . <p> Underneath , someone wrote : " I just tried lifting some weights , sprinting and jumping , as you advised . I 'm in A&amp;E now and a consultant will be down to see me shortly . " <p> A joke , undoubtedly . Yet this is a concerningly common belief : exercise will hurt me , I dare not do it . <p> It also demonstrates a misunderstanding of the two fundamental principles @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ principles , they will keep you in enviable shape for the rest of your life . Below , I 'm going to share them with you . <h> The first secret to successful exercise : identify your capabilities and get started <p> We should only tackle exercises that sit within our capabilities . That is how we avoid overstretching ourselves and suffering an injury . <p> Everyone has different capabilities . Elite athletes might be able to run 100 miles or chuck 200kg over their head , while a less fit person who leads a busy life might struggle to run a mile or lift a light dumbbell . <p> However , while everyone has different capabilities , the most important thing to note is that everyone is capable of something . <p> If you ca n't sprint , you run . If you ca n't run , you walk . If you ca n't walk , you might try low-impact alternatives like swimming , or exercise machines which use other muscles to raise your heart rate . <p> Often , people assume doing these more accessible variations of an @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ could n't be further from the truth . <p> A new meta-analysis found that people experienced a disproportionate amount of muscle growth in their first few months of strength training . As time went on , results continued , but at a reduced rate . This phenomenon often extends to many other health markers too , filed under the phrase " newbie gains " . <p> The key take home message here is that simply starting to exercise , in whatever form works for you , holds immense value . <p> As Dr Stuart Phillips of the American College of Sports Medicine puts it : " Training all major muscle groups at least twice a week matters far more than chasing the idea of a ' perfect ' or complex training plan . Whether it 's barbells , bands or body weight exercises , consistency and effort drive results . " <h> The second secret to successful exercise : apply progressive overload <p> The other thing this meta-analysis highlights is , once you are into the swing of things with your exercise routine , you need to apply some form @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ progressive overload , and it is the second key principle behind any successful exercise plan . <p> General movement in any form will be beneficial for your health . But for certain fitness perks such as increasing cardiorespiratory fitness , there comes a point where you have to challenge yourself every once in a while . <p> But again , this does n't mean suddenly running a marathon , sprinting 100m in sub-10 seconds or hoiking 100-plus kilograms from the floor . It just means gradually upping the difficulty of your workouts in line with your increasing fitness levels . <p> If I walked 10 minutes each day last week and it felt easy , I might walk 11 minutes each day this week , or consciously up my pace ever so slightly . <p> If I felt comfortable doing three sets of 10 goblet squats with a 12kg kettlebell last week , resting 60 seconds between each set , I might do three sets of 12 repetitions this week . <p> If I ran 5km in 30 minutes last week , this week I might try to run 1km @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ rest for a few minutes , then repeat this four more times . This way , I have practiced running the same distance in less time . <p> In each scenario , I tweaked variables in my workouts to make them slightly more challenging -- either by increasing the amount of work I 'm doing or raising the intensity of the task . <p> The key is to stay within your capabilities , but try to experience the upper end . Doing this will widen your capability window -- or , in simpler terms , make you fitter . <p> The reason this works is called the SAID principle , which stands for specific adaptations to imposed demands . This means the body will , handily , adapt to be better at the things you consistently do . <p> Regular aerobic exercise like running will likely result in a more efficient heart and lungs . Regular strength training will likely result in stronger muscles , bones , ligaments and tendons , among other perks . <p> But to trigger these adaptations , you have to put a persuasive business case @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ appropriately challenging workout sends .

@@139297423 <p> The contentious issue of data centers -- and their impact on the environment and local communities -- continues to make headlines , as the need for more computing power comes up against concerns about whether that extra capacity is worth the cost . <p> One of the natural resources that data centers need is water , and plenty of it , to cool down the chips running calculations . There 's a lot of variation in the statistics used to measure it , for all kinds of reasons : data centers water usage can vary significantly from site to site , for example , and there 's also the question of what counts as water usage . <p> Should the water needed to generate the electricity to power a data center be included , or not ? By which I mean : Bournemouth before it was ruined . As such , it 's the kind of place that usually calls for a return visit . My calendar was empty , I already had a hired car and I was keen to explore a part of France I 've never seen before -- the French Atlantic coast between Brittany and Bayonne . <p> The only fly in the ointment was the weather forecast . When I turned to my sensible AI -- NinaGPT -- to construct a coastal itinerary , she kept saying " Are you sure you want to do this Sean , there is a heatwave coming . " I scolded her for being a nanny and laughingly reminded her I 'm a travel veteran ; I like hot sunny weather and I 've been to several war zones . I set off . <p> Major mistake . One afternoon , parked by an Aldi west of Conques , @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ car registered the intensifying heat : 116F , 118F , 120F . I actually took photographs . It was surely not that hot in reality : car thermometers are unreliable , especially if you 're sitting on baked tarmac . Nonetheless it was indicative of the heat dome settling over France . It also reminded me of the last time I 'd stared at a car thermometer in wary amazement . That was in the Fish River Canyon in southern Namibia . That time , my car told me it was 115F . I took a photograph then , as well . <p> By the time I reached sun-struck Moissac the heatwave was near its raging peak . I quickly learned the French for this phenomenon : canicule . I also learned the sobering truth that much of provincial France lacks air conditioning . Its buildings rely on shutters , thick walls and ventilation ; defenses which begin to fail above 95F . In the main square of Moissac I scurried to a shady but uncooled brasserie to bash out an article . The sweat dripped from my nose onto @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ Macron warned that the " hottest day in French history " was approaching . <p> It came as I arrived in Arcachon . I 'd booked an apartment , right on the beach , which looked suitably modern . I figured sea breezes plus air conditioning would see me through the worst . As I pulled up , around 6pm , it was a brutal , stifling 102F . There was no sea breeze . The sea in the bay looked sad and listless , repressed by a despotic sun . To top it all off , even here there was no air conditioning . <p> I had n't checked the small print . Stupidly I 'd just assumed the flat would be properly kitted out , because it was so clearly brand new . Not only did it have no air conditioning , but it also had no fans and no through breeze . It was maybe 122F in the punishment block of the bedroom . My reservation was non-refundable but I kicked up such a fuss on Booking.com 's helpline -- " I could die in there " @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ a refund . I used the money to find a grand hotel with climatisation . And then I hid . <p> Because that is all you can do when the thermometer soars over 104F . Hide . Shelter in place . It is like sitting out an air raid , or a hurricane , except it goes on for longer . Every time I did venture out , I got an instant pounding headache and I hurried back inside . <p> It was a truly horrible experience , and I write as someone who has been through severe heat . I 've been in Luxor , Egypt when it hit 109F , I 've been in Death Valley , Eastern California during similar . Somehow , they were more tolerable than Arcachon , France during the recent canicule . Perhaps because you expect great heat in deserts but not in the suburbs of Bordeaux ; perhaps because the proximity of the sea added humidity . <p> French buildings rely on shutters , thick walls and ventilation ; defenses which begin to fail above 95F <p> I 've had just one @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ the Danakil Depression , Ethiopia . But it 's not just the temperature that echoed : in both places I had the sensation of being trapped and tormented . Of suffering inescapably . And the mud huts had no air conditioning . <p> The obvious question arises . If these heatwaves continue , and worsen , what will they do to Europe , and European life ? No one can be certain , but I remember my charming , capricious Auntie Lois , who spent her life shifting nervously around the world . At one point she fled Los Angeles after an earthquake . At the time I put it down to her highly-strung nature ; an over-reaction . And yet I now think of her explanation , " The earthquake changed the way I felt about California . I felt like my home was turning on me , that the ground @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ Europe will be fine , we will briskly adapt -- and install air conditioning everywhere . That 's what I used to believe . Certainly , there are only so many times you can experience an earthquake before you think -- that 's it , I 'm out of here , and I 'm not coming back . Especially not for summer holidays . @@139334365 <h> Why are thousands of mosquitoes being released in Washington DC ? <p> About 600,000 mosquitoes are being released across the Washington DC area this summer to help reduce local mosquito populations . Only male mosquitoes -- infected with the naturally occurring bacteria Wolbachia -- are released . They do n't bite humans , and the bacteria they carry prevents any eggs produced after mating from hatching . <p> Bee Safe Mosquito Control is the first business in the US to offer this form of pest control directly to residents . Historically , only local government mosquito control districts , public health agencies , or research partnerships have done so . <p> But the method is now gaining popularity , with Alphabet , Google 's parent company , seeking approval to release up to 64 million Wolbachia-infected mosquitoes in California and Florida . The effort comes as climate change creates more favourable conditions for mosquitoes to survive and reproduce , increasing concerns about the spread of mosquito-borne diseases .

@@139349912 <h> Share <h> Three cheers for Britain 's most unabashedly elitist school <p> As we ponder the ups and downs of the UK 's sporting record this summer , it might be worth noting their unquestioned prowess when it comes to the demands of classically based dancing . The Royal Ballet is consistently more than a match for any comparable company in the world , and its chief feeder , the Royal Ballet School , currently celebrating its centenary , is similarly and solidly rated as one of the two or three best of its kind anywhere . <p> Both these institutions are deeply beholden to tradition , and the RBS might well be the most unabashedly elitist educational establishment in the country . It receives globally more than 2,500 applications a year . All these will lead to an audition , the number finally whittled down to 30-odd offers of a full-time place . For a nice change , merit and potential are strictly the only criteria in a rigorous selection process ( entirely misrepresented in the film and musical Billy Elliot ) . About half its 200-odd students @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ are British citizens . The great majority receive substantial scholarships , financed via the government and private donors . <p> The RBS is divided between a junior section housed in White Lodge in Richmond Park and a senior section next to the Royal Opera House ; recent inspection reports are highly favorable , both academically and pastorally -- " all the relevant standards are met " -- and it undoubtedly comes up with the goods , inasmuch as virtually all its final-year graduates end up with a professional placement . <p> The Royal Ballet School is not a place for sissies : nobody there is going to be mollycoddled <p> The RBS is , however , extremely defensive of its reputation and cagey about granting outsiders access . In the recent past there have been accusations that the draconian drill and repetition necessary to instill balletic technique can degenerate into thoughtless cruelty . The stress and competition certainly gets dangerously intense , particularly for children who are n't maturing physically in the right way and for their own good need to be periodically " assessed out " -- in other @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ for eating disorders , always a concern among teenage girls , but especially so among aspiring ballerinas . Given the amount of close contact dance involves , guarding against sexual abuse is also a sensitive matter . <p> Five years ago , in the wake of the hushed-up suicide of the choreographer Liam Scarlett , these and other issues were discomfortingly aired in a whistleblowing article by Luke Jennings in the London Review of Books , followed in 2023 by a BBC Panorama documentary , luridly entitled The Dark Side of Ballet Schools . The evidence presented included submissions by some who simply had n't made the grade , and there was a whiff of sour grapes in their accounts of the way they had been bullied and demoralized . But the RBS is not a place for sissies : nobody there is going to be mollycoddled . <p> Leadership today is tripartite . In the past , emphases in the curriculum have been the source of considerable friction , as school directors such as Dame Merle Park and Gailene Stock promoted ideas that did n't align with what the Royal Ballet -- the school 's primary target -- required . The present incumbent is Iain Mackay , himself once a student at the RBS and a former principal of Birmingham Royal Ballet . Only two years into the job , he is both personable and plausible , but he has already made a radical change that could have a far-reaching impact . ( He refused a request for an interview . ) <p> Beginning this fall , the school will raise its starting age for full-time boarders from 11 to 12 . Year 7 students will train through a new network of regional hubs , building on existing plans . @@139405556 <h> Social media driving wild animal pet trade <p> This is not a trade that 's happening in faraway places under a veil of secrecy . <p> Social media has become a single global marketplace for the wild animal pet trade . <p> The platforms are the marketplace , the algorithms are the marketing , and millions of everyday interactions , from likes and shares to comments and follows , can unintentionally fuel demand for wild animals as pets . <p> New research supports this too . The Association of Zoos and Aquariums ( AZA ) , the International Fund for Animal Welfare ( IFAW ) and World Wildlife Fund ( WWF ) recently published a report , ' Primates for Purchase ' . <p> Over in Europe , IFAW 's ' Liked to death ' campaign and report link the " cute " social media content we see in our feeds to what we do n't see : the suffering of wild animals traded and kept as pets . <p> Two pieces of research from either side of the Atlantic , both telling us the same story of the @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ crisis . Animals are under growing pressure from habitat destruction , climate change , and poaching , and nearly three-quarters of the world 's primate species are now threatened with extinction . However , there is another factor that is often overlooked : the wild animal pet trade . <p> Trafficking <p> African grey parrot populations have declined by around 90 per cent in some regions over the past 50 years , largely because of the pet trade . <p> It is therefore one of the world 's largest illicit markets . Increasingly , this is now being done using mobile phones . <p> The data shows this is not a problem confined to one country . The US ' Primates for Purchase ' study found 1,614 primates listed for sale in just six weeks across Facebook , Instagram , TikTok , and YouTube , with 21 of those listings linked to UK locations . <p> Yet awareness in Europe lags far behind the scale of the problem . The ' Liked to death ' EU report found that while 82 per cent of Europeans surveyed see wildlife trafficking as @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ that Europe is one of its major hubs . <p> Enforcement <p> In the UK , IFAW 's ' Behind Closed Doors ' survey of wild pet owners found 54 per cent did n't know whether their pet required a licence and , among those who did , 84 per cent did not have one . <p> This is not a trade that 's happening in faraway places under a veil of secrecy . <p> This is not a trade that 's happening in faraway places under a veil of secrecy . It 's happening right in front of us , on our own screens , close to home . <p> The wild animal pet trade now operates as a single global marketplace , running on the same major social media platforms on both sides of the Atlantic . <p> Reels , pictures and feeds connect buyers and sellers across borders , while the lack of effective regulation , or of its enforcement , lets illegal trade flourish and reinforces the dangerous idea that wild animals make suitable pets . <p> The methods used by sellers are similar wherever they @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ " rehoming , " " adoption fees " and " rescue " to evade platform filters . <p> Buyers are directed off platforms onto WhatsApp or Direct Messages ( DMs ) to complete the transaction . Emojis stand in for species names to avoid automated detection . <p> The language a trafficker uses to sell a macaque in Florida is the language they use to sell an African grey parrot in France . Most social media users have no idea this activity is taking place around them , yet many encounter and engage with the content that helps sustain it . <p> Public opinion is well ahead of the politicians on this . The ' Liked to death ' European survey found that 84 per cent of Europeans surveyed support stronger wildlife protection laws . <p> Laundered <p> More surprisingly , IFAW 's ' Behind Closed Doors ' research found that 68 per cent of UK wild pet owners support stricter regulation , including the listing of which species are allowed to be traded ( the so-called ' positive list system ' ) , while 79 per cent say they @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ When the people who own wild animals are calling for tighter rules , the case for action is hard to ignore . Although the data demonstrates public advocacy , legislation has yet to catch up with the rapidly evolving platforms . <p> The pressure is now on European policy makers to catch up , and the ' Liked to death ' campaign sets out three clear places to start . <p> First , the UK and EU should adopt positive lists identifying which species can legally be kept as pets . This shifts the burden of proof onto sellers rather than enforcement agencies , and clarifies the rules to consumers , traders and police alike . <p> Second , the import , trade , and possession of any species protected in its country of origin should be criminalised . Wildlife stolen abroad must not be quietly laundered into a European market through legal loopholes . <p> Unfolding <p> Third , platform obligations under the EU Digital Services Act ( DSA ) need to be properly enforced , with real consequences when illegal listings are reported and ignored . <p> IFAW @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ Trusted Flagger under the DSA , a status formally recognising its expertise in identifying illegal wildlife trade content online and reporting it to platforms . Yet one in four of the listings it flagged to platforms last year was either rejected or ignored . The framework exists , but what is missing is enforcement . <p> A buyer in the US , Britain , or anywhere in Europe no longer needs detective skills or back-alley connections to find a wild animal for sale . They need only a phone , a social media account and a few seconds of attention . <p> Every like , every comment , every share tells the algorithm to surface more of the same , turning a single trafficker 's post into a global marketing campaign .
